dedupe_keys.name: clarc customizable artificial community for modelling extreme hazard effects on interdependent civil infrastructure

description: CLARC is an artificial coastal community of about 500,000 people over some 1,065 square miles, built for modelling how extreme hazard events propagate through interdependent civil infrastructure. It contains five civil infrastructure networks (electricity, water, wastewater, transportation and communications), social infrastructure such as public safety and healthcare, population and socio-economic attributes, and the interdependencies between the networks and between civil and social infrastructure. Researchers led by Loggins, Sharkey and Wallace produced it with US Department of Homeland Security funding and published it on DesignSafe-CI in December 2018 as a 367 MB Microsoft Access database with an overview PDF, available as a free download under ODC-BY 1.0. Coverage is a single synthetic site, not a real place. Caveats: the Access format needs conversion for most tools and the community has not been updated since 2018. Simulation uses: a shared testbed for cascading failure, restoration optimisation, resilience and emergency response models across water, wastewater and other networks. Related records: HIFLD Open (data-hifld-open) and the Exeter water network benchmarks (data-exeter-cws-water-network-benchmarks).
